title: "The Cathedral and the Bazaar" and the Open-Source Argument (1997)
explainer: In 1997, programmer Eric S. Raymond presented "The Cathedral and the Bazaar," drawing on his own experience maintaining the Fetchmail mail utility to argue that open, many-contributor "bazaar"-style development could produce more robust software than the closed, tightly controlled "cathedral" model of small core teams. The essay was cited internally at Netscape as part of the reasoning behind its 1998 decision to release the source code for its browser, an event often treated as a founding moment of the modern open-source movement — and the underlying argument for why letting outside contributors submit patches upstream is a strength rather than a risk.
